title: Head of Project Control em espírito santo (RN)
description:
About us

Hanseatic Global Terminals (HGT) is a fully owned subsidiary of Hapag-Lloyd. Operating from Rotterdam, HGT manages a portfolio of stakes in 231 terminals and complementary logistics services across 11 countries across 5 continents: Europe, North America, South America, Asia, Africa – with plans to expand its stakes to ~30 terminals by 2030.

Spanning key regions, its portfolio comprises port terminals and related logistics services operated by Hanseatic Global Terminals Latin America in Latin America and Florida (USA), and, in the booming Indian market, it is present through the container terminals, depots and rail business of J M Baxi, India’s largest integrated terminal and logistics provider. Additionally, HGT’s presence in strategic European hubs, such as Germany, France and the Mediterranean, enhances its global network and allows it to offer seamless, efficient logistics and supply chain solutions to customers worldwide.

At HGT, we are a highly motivated team of experienced international professionals who believe that growth in any partnership comes from trust and dedication. Our commitment to provide highly efficient terminal operations that are safe, sustainable, and reliable is rooted in a simple yet powerful vision: “offering exceptional service quality at all times.”

The project: Hanseatic Global Terminals Aracruz port terminal:

Hanseatic Global Terminals (HGT) is embarking on an exciting new chapter with the development of Hanseatic Global Terminals Aracruz, a state‑of‑the‑art container terminal created in partnership with the Imetame Group. Following HGT’s recent agreement to acquire 50% of the shares in Imetame Logística Porto (ILP), this joint venture marks a significant strategic investment in Brazil’s evolving port landscape and will play a key role in strengthening global supply chain connectivity.

Located in Aracruz, Espírito Santo, the new terminal is designed to be a modern transshipment and gateway hub for the region. Expected to launch operations by mid‑2028, the facility will feature a capacity of approximately 1.2 million TEU, 750 meters of quay, advanced cargo‑handling technology, and 17 meters of water depth, enabling the efficient handling of the industry’s largest vessels.

As HGT and the Imetame Group work together to build and operate this future‑ready terminal, we are assembling a team of talented professionals who will help shape the next major milestone in Brazil’s port infrastructure development. The project represents an opportunity to be part of a transformational venture that will set new standards for performance, innovation, and operational excellence.

The position

The Head of Project Control is responsible for creating a clear and trusted view of project performance by ensuring accurate, timely, and transparent communication across internal teams and external stakeholders. This role brings project management excellence to the forefront by applying best practices, and tools, to support strong decision making and maintain focus on customer value as it evolves. At the same time, the Head of Project Controls cultivates a proactive, insight‑driven project environment by using leading and lagging indicators to anticipate risks early, highlight improvement opportunities, and guide the project consistently toward successful outcomes.

Success requires transparency, deep expertise, and a forward‑looking mindset that continuously predicts, improves, and strengthens project performance.

Key Responsibilities

General

  • Implement, maintain, and champion the transparent use of HGT project management and control tools across the project team, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.
  • Establish and maintain the project’s scope, schedule, quality, and budget baselines.
  • Facilitate:
    • Effective application of core project governance processes, including change management, scope, schedule, requirements, and budget changes.
    • Risk management, ensuring timely input and ownership from the project team.
    • Document Management and correspondence registration system
  • Monitor progress against approved baselines and ensure that deviations are identified early, addressed promptly, and escalated or reported when necessary.
  • Ensure correct and timely project performance reporting:
    • within the project and team.
    • to Project Director and other relevant project leaders.
    • to Head Office.
    • to other corporate counterparts (as required).

Communication

  • Function as primary point of contact for all project control systems and be responsible for the user rights administration.
  • Liaise with the functional counterpart on project control system issues and improvements.
  • Hold regular touchpoints with construction, equipment, IT and finance teams to stay ahead of potential project control issues.
  • Build and sustain strong working relationships with head office counterparts, consultants, contractors, and suppliers.

Interfaces

  • Work closely with all project disciplines to ensure consistent, accurate, and coordinated project controls.
  • Liaise with relevant HGT global departments to maintain alignment with company standards and best practices.

Job requirements

  • Relevant professional experience: 10 years overall, including a minimum of 5 years within a project controls functional discipline.
  • Holding a bachelor’s degree (or relevant).
  • Working in a cultural and technical diverse team and environment, internally and externally to your organization.
  • Confidently present and communicate with internal project teams and external HQ stakeholders in both written and spoken English and Portuguese.
  • Coach, mentor, and support others across the project team or wider functional areas.
  • Demonstrate relevant, practical technical experience and knowledge in project controls and project management disciplines.
  • Delivering a high‑level of accuracy and quality.
  • Hold an advanced project management qualification, such as APM PMQ, PMI PMP, or an equivalent certification.
  • Proficient in project management platforms and systems used for document control, contract management, change control, cost management, communications, and milestone tracking (e.g., Aconex, PMWeb, PCM, Skire, or similar).
  • Skilled in project management and scheduling tools such as Primavera Cloud, Primavera P6, MS Project, or equivalent.
  • Experience supervising or line‑managing others in project controls or project management roles.

What we offer

  • Competitive salary and benefits package.
  • Opportunity to shape the global footprint of a fast‑growing terminal operator.
  • High‑impact leadership role in a dynamic, global, and collaborative organization.

title: Salesforce Solutions Architect (Manufacturing Cloud and Agentforce) - Contractor (Remote) em estados unidos (PI)
description:
About Us: At DX Foundation, where we're not just Salesforce consultants - we're architects of the digital future. Our mission is to empower businesses to unlock the full potential of their customer relationships through innovative digital experiences.

As a cross‑cloud Salesforce partner with a focus, our focus isn't just on technology - it's on crafting a digital journey that enhances customer, user, and IT experiences. We lead with advisory services, ingraining best practices and strategic thinking into every implementation. At DXF, we specialize in elevating the Salesforce experience for businesses of all sizes. Our core expertise lies in integrating strategic advisory, best practices, and tailored strategies into every Salesforce implementation. By focusing on the overall digital experience, we ensure that the solutions we provide are not just technically sound but also enhance the customer and user journey.

We are seeking an experienced Senior Salesforce Solutions Architect with deep expertise in Manufacturing Cloud and Agentforce to lead the architectural design and delivery of a standardized Land & Expand (Account Management) playbook for a multi‑org Salesforce environment in the manufacturing and industrial services sector.

This high‑visibility engagement requires building a simple, highly adoptable foundation focused on data hygiene and account management processes for users with low CRM maturity. The solution must emphasize decoupled architecture to support future M&A flexibility while enabling standardized reporting and visibility into recurring / installed‑base revenue across a portfolio of independent orgs.

You will architect a repeatable "Crawl" phase solution centered on guided workflows, Asset tracking, and expansion opportunity management that can be efficiently stamped out across multiple Sales Cloud Enterprise orgs. If you have successfully delivered Manufacturing Cloud extensions, Agentforce implementations, and simple guided user experiences for frontline manufacturing or industrial sales teams, we want to hear from you.

This is a contractor position with a competitive rate of $80–$120 USD per hour, based on experience and qualifications.

What You Will Do

  • Lead the architectural design and delivery of a standardized Land & Expand Playbook built on Manufacturing Cloud capabilities, extending Sales Cloud to support account management, installed‑base visibility, and expansion revenue tracking.
  • Design and implement the Crawl‑phase foundation using guided Screen Flows (Deal Wizard style) to drive simple data capture, opportunity hygiene, and Asset creation for recurring and recurring revenue visibility.
  • Architect clean separation between New Business ("Hunting") and Account Management ("Farming") processes, leveraging Manufacturing Cloud objects (Assets, Entitlements, Contracts, Work Orders where applicable) and custom extensions while maintaining simplicity.
  • Build a templated, repeatable solution (configuration + packageable components) that supports efficient deployment across multiple independent orgs with controlled, industry‑appropriate variations.
  • Incorporate Agentforce agents to automate repetitive tasks, provide guided prompts, and support low‑maturity users in account planning and expansion opportunity management.
  • Design lightweight, guided Account Planning experiences using Screen Flows and Agentforce to improve adoption without adding complexity.
  • Ensure the architecture remains fully decoupled for M&A flexibility (no cross‑org automation dependencies) while feeding aggregated data into a central reporting layer via Data Cloud.
  • Provide technical leadership to onshore delivery teams (developers, admins, QA) ensuring solutions follow Salesforce best practices, security, performance, and governance standards while prioritizing radical simplicity for end‑user adoption.
  • Collaborate with the Principal Consultant and client stakeholders to align architecture decisions with business objectives around revenue growth from existing accounts and operational standardization.
  • Produce and maintain architecture diagrams, data models, solution blueprints, deployment playbooks, and low‑code component documentation.
  • Support agile delivery with all onshore resources in 2‑week sprints, including discovery refinement, design reviews, sprint planning, and client‑facing demos.
  • Advise on license strategy, user growth (including inside sales roles), and change management considerations for low‑maturity manufacturing/industrial teams.
  • Architect Integration Solutions: Design and develop detailed integration architectures and workflows using Mulesoft's Anypoint Platform to align with business objectives, integrating systems such as Salesforce, Snowflake, AWS, SAP, SharePoint, and external applications.
  • Develop Mule Flows: Create Mule ESB projects using connectors (Salesforce, File, Database, AMQ, SMTP, Transformers, DataWeave) for both on‑premises and cloud‑hosted applications, utilizing synchronous and asynchronous flows.

Position Title: Building Quality Coach – Central ND

Decision‑making authority: Responsible for best interests of SEEC within budget; approvals required from Director of Student Services or designee for specific matters.

Position Overview

The Building Quality Coach is an external coach providing technical supervision and coaching support to early childhood providers and center staff across the eight human service regions. The role involves coaching, modeling evidence‑based best practices, and supporting the SEEC’s overall goals, objectives, and strategies.

Key Job Duties

  • Support implementation of evidence‑based Building Quality Initiatives (e.g., SEEDS for 3‑5 year olds, SEEDS for infants & toddlers, SEEDS for family child care, Pyramid Model, math & science skills). Assist educators with social, emotional, language, and literacy development.
  • Conduct classroom/program observations, provide coaching, and collect data to recommend continuous improvement across health and safety, child development, social and emotional, literacy, numeracy, and supportive environments.
  • Help providers develop SMART goals and support progress. Offer feedback, time for reflection, and promote goal setting.
  • Assist sites in data‑based decision making by reviewing assessment practices and recommending data collection and progress monitoring strategies.
  • Create supporting resources such as fidelity checklists aligned to licensing and early childhood standards.
  • Collaborate with CCA staff to communicate areas of improvement and professional development needs based on observation data.
  • Consult with center staff on early childhood instruction, assessment, and intervention; model, observe, provide corrective feedback, solve challenges, exercise sound judgment.
  • Audit, develop, and facilitate trainings that support child care programs and providers statewide.
  • In conjunction with the Director of Student Services, review current programs and identify growth opportunities aligned to agency strategic goals.
  • Build and extend own knowledge through professional development (webinars, training, certifications).

Essential Skills, Experience, and Expertise

  • BS/BA in Early Childhood Education or Child Development OR bachelor’s degree in related field with ≥24 semester credits in Early Childhood Education. Alternatively, bachelor’s or higher degree in unrelated field with ≥24 semester credits in Early Childhood Education AND a valid ND Teaching License in Pre‑K–K or K‑3.
  • Valid ND Growing Futures Building Quality Coach endorsement (current or to be obtained within 30 days).
  • Experience facilitating adult learners through training, coaching, supervision, and observation.
  • Exceptional interpersonal skills for effective communication and problem‑solving with the early childhood field.
  • Strong flexibility, adaptability, and self‑initiative with independent follow‑through.
  • Knowledge of early childhood settings and a desire for ongoing professional development.
  • Confidentiality: Proper protection, handling, storage, and disposal of PII.
  • Math skills: addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages, fractions, basic descriptive statistics.
  • Financial management and analysis: develop, track, analyze, and explain budgets and variances.
  • Presentation and speaking skills: deliver effective small and large group presentations.
  • Reading and writing: college‑level analysis, synthesis, and evaluation per Bloom’s taxonomy.
  • Driver’s license required; up to 50% travel within regional area, including occasional overnight travel.
  • Tech proficiency: smartphones, tablets, cloud‑based apps, Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), QuickBooks, document management.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

  • High level of interaction with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet deadlines with professional demeanor.
  • Stand/Walk/stand/office activity: up to 8–10 hours per day.
  • Lift up to 25 pounds.
  • Work environments: typical office temperatures 60–85 °F; occasional outdoor work in temperatures ranging from –40 °F to 110 °F.
  • Noise levels typical of office; may require hearing protection when using certain equipment.
  • Exposure to small quantities of hazardous office chemicals (toner, glue).

Special Position Requirements

  • Travel: up to 50% travel within regional area for site observations and coaching; occasional overnight travel for visits or professional development.
  • Professional attire for positive impression on staff, clients, stakeholders, board members, and partners.

Accountabilities, Responsibilities, and Essential Functions

Achieve performance goals while maintaining high levels of customer satisfaction. Build positive internal and external relationships, adhere to legal, compliance, and departmental standards, and coordinate work to avoid last‑minute confusion.

  • Garantir a utilização eficaz de sistemas e ferramentas de monitoramento e controle operacional, assegurando a confiabilidade das informações e a pronta resposta a situações críticas.
  • Promover a cultura de segurança operacional, excelência técnica e melhoria contínua no âmbito do COI, incentivando práticas que reduzam riscos e elevem o nível de desempenho operacional.

  • Experiência no desenvolvimento, implementação e gestão de indicadores técnicos e comerciais, com foco na eficiência operacional, continuidade e qualidade do fornecimento de energia.
  • Experiência na representação institucional da empresa em comitês técnicos, audiências judiciais e interações com órgãos reguladores e entidades do setor elétrico, assegurando a adequada defesa dos interesses operacionais da companhia.

  • Conhecimento em gestão de processos operacionais, elaboração de relatórios técnicos, análise de indicadores e avaliação de desempenho do sistema elétrico.

description:
Accountable to: Executive Director

Department: Special Education

FLSAStatus: Full-Time Exempt

EmployeesundertheirDirectSupervision: Seethe mostcurrentorganizationalchartfordirectandindirect reports under thisleader.

Standard Office Hours: Nine-month position; typically working Monday-Friday, 8:00 am to 4:00 pm, and other times as needed to reach agency goals or job duties.

Decision Making Authority: Responsible for the best interests of the South East Education Cooperative (SEEC) given what has been budgeted and carefully utilizes funding to achieve expected goals. Approval required from the Executive Director (or assigned designee) on specific matters as outlined in policies and procedures.

Position Overview

Responsible to evaluate students to determine their functional levels and identify special needs. Plan, implement, evaluate and document therapeutic activities to assist students to benefit from their educational experiences. Provide leadership and assistance for the Medicaid enrollment and use process for service providers, parents and students. Responsible for representing the SEEC in a positive way to staff and member schools. Supports the overall goals, objectives and strategies of the SEEC.

Position Accountabilities, Responsibilities and Essential Functions

A critical part of every position is achieving the goals set for the position while delivering high levels of satisfaction to internal and external stakeholders. This is realized by building positive internal individual and team relationships, positive relationships with external partners and exhibiting behaviors that contribute to the success of short and long-term goals of the agency. These behaviors include a focus on timely completion and high quality of work (with or without supervision) while following all legal, compliance, departmental, documentation, safety, timelines, program and other standards per company policies and procedures. Position requires close collaboration with Executive Director, teachers, students, SEEC Employees in addition to Community and Funding Agencies. Performance is equally a function of goal attainment; timely and accurate completion of assignments; building positive internal and external relationships; and planning, communicating and coordinating work to avoid last minute confusion and adherence legal/compliance guidelines and policies/procedures.

Significant Job Duties

  • 85% Program Management: Speech Therapy
    • Provide treatment and work on skills with students to include, but not limited to, articulation, speech development, and language development
    • Conduct initial evaluations on students referred to Speech Therapy along with reevaluations of students when necessary.
    • Responsible for program planning, management and implementation to meet the goals of the student Individual Education Plan (IEP).
    • Function as a team member for assigned IEPs and collaborate with education staff, family, physicians and agencies.
    • Collaborate with teachers and staff to schedule Speech sessions and to check on student progress in the classroom. Provide recommendations for teachers and staff when necessary.
    • Obtain needed equipment and materials for students that assist them in participating in daily school activities.
    • Responsible for completing all required documentation concerning the Speech program including, but not limited to, Medicaid billing for students who use Speech services.
    • Proper and ethical managing of assigned grant funding including expenditure approvals to established limit, budgeting and grant reporting to meet established expectations/metrics.
    • In conjunction with Executive Director, review program trends, data and funding to provide input and/or write future grant application(s) following agency policies.
    • Manage assigned program area(s) in a business-like and disciplined manner that includes administration and evaluation consistent with best practices.
    • Communicate the value, results and effectiveness of services provided to enhance continuous improvement.
  • 5% Legal, Compliance and Safety Programs
    • Supports agency approved policies and best practices that ensure effective and efficient
  • 5% Sustain Long Term Viability and Growth
    • In conjunction with the Executive, review the current Speech programs and identify potential opportunities that align to the agency's strategic goals.
  • 5% Professional Development
    • Build and extend own knowledge through a variety of professional development activities
    • including but not limited to webinars, training classes, special certifications and by engaging in other professional development activities.

Physical Demands and Work Environment

  • Interaction levels with others: Requires high levels of interactions with others internal and external to the agency.
  • Position requires travel within the SEEC service area, North Dakota and beyond to fulfill job goals. If not traveling, work location is in Fargo at the SEEC office.
  • Ability to work under pressure and deadlines while maintaining professional demeanor.
  • Alternative schedules and overtime expectations are frequent.
  • Sit / Stand / Walk / Stoop: Up to 8-10 hours a day for each activity individually or combined.
  • Use of Phone/ Computer /Software / Office Equipment: Up to 8-10 hours a day for each activity individually or combined.
  • Climb / Pull / Lift: Up to 8-10 hours a day for each activity individually or combined. Move and lift up to 25 pounds.
  • Temperatures ranges for work environment: Mostly a typical office environment and temperatures of 60-85°F, but can experience temperatures from -40 °F to 110°F when performing tasks outside of office.
  • Noise: Noise levels reflect typical office environment and may require hearing protection when using certain equipment or entering certain areas.
  • Hazardous Conditions or Chemicals Exposure: Exposure to small quantities of hazardous chemicals found in office supplies such as toner, glues, etc.

Essential Skills, Experience and Expertise

  • Education: Master's degree in Speech Therapy, current ESPB Speech Therapy License, ASHA certification and current ND Board of Speech, Audiology and Hearing license.
  • Action oriented, entrepreneurial and innovative approach to service delivery.
  • Interpersonal and Communication Skills: Requires excellent customer service and interpersonal communication skills. Able to effectively collaborate with diverse groups and develop high performing teams; yet smoothly manages individual and group conflicts. Handles pressure and keeps calm when faced with competing demands and priorities.
  • Attention to Detail/Organization and Short/Long Range Planning: Excellent skills required.
  • Confidentially: Requires proper protection, handling, storage and disposal of confidential and personally identifiable information (PII).
  • Math Skills: Adept at addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, percentages, fractions and basic descriptive statistics.
  • Presentations / Speaking skills: Can develop and deliver effective small and large group presentations to a variety of stakeholders.
  • Reading and Writing Skills: College Level: Requires analysis, synthesis and evaluation skills in a variety of areas per Bloom's taxonomy.
  • Driver's License: Required.
  • Use of software and office equipment: Ability to use smart phones and tablets, cloud based and internet apps, standard office equipment (copier, fax etc), computers, Microsoft office, other specialized software and the internet. Working knowledge of Word, Excel and PowerPoint to create and alter documentations, forms, presentations and graphs. Able to retrieve / store documents on computer (desktop/laptop), shared site or on cloud based service.
  • Travel: No overnight travel but potential 25% travel primarily within North Dakota.
  • Clothing: Professional attire that creates positive impression on staff, stakeholders, Board Members and funding or partner organizations.

This role combines strong people leadership with hands‑on commercial execution, acting as a key link between strategy and day‑to‑day delivery.

Consumer Experience & Engagement

  • Support adoption of digital sales tools and data‑driven selling practices.

Cross‑Functional Collaboration

  • Proven ability to deliver sales targets through effective team leadership and execution.
  • Experience working within structured sales processes and commercial frameworks.
  • Strong customer focus with an understanding of the end‑to‑end consumer sales journey.
  • Comfortable translating strategy into clear, practical actions for teams.
  • Strong communication, coaching, and stakeholder management skills.
  • Data‑driven mindset with experience using performance metrics to guide decisions.
  • Ability to operate effectively in a fast‑paced, evolving environment.
